engagement_title: Maison Valcere fine-jewellery house, first season under one identity: bring two bench sessions to one house look, recover the wordmark off a printed swing tag, and carry both onto the house-story deck, the A2 poster directions, the boutique tiles and a spec card for every reference in the book
vertical: Jewelry, watches and accessories: an independent four-person fine-jewellery house, appointment-led boutique above a bookshop plus a small stockist channel (Montreal, Quebec)
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Freelancer.com post 'Luxury E-commerce Brand Visuals' quoted in the ledger, for an independent high-jewellery identity that 'must feel unmistakably premium', built on a deep-black canvas with crisp white typography, 'purely typographic, no symbols, icons or complex marks', a strict monochrome palette, and usage rules so 'every asset, from product packaging to video title cards, stays consistent'. Co-anchor one: the Freelancer.com sterling-silver post asking for 'clean, consistent imagery for our online catalogue and marketplaces' so 'the metalwork stays the hero', every file on a pure white ground with no visible shadows or colour cast, delivered as high-resolution images plus a per-product catalogue. Co-anchor two: the Upwork men's-accessories post whose client wanted catalogue material its design team could run 'refinements and iterations' against, and factory-ready files for its manufacturing partners. The house is the coined fictional Maison Valcere; no real company, person, product or trademark is named, and the palette names are invented. REPOSITIONED for connector reality: the original posts imply a physical shoot and 3D CAD, neither of which is connector work, while CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) changes what the honest fuller commission is, because HTML authoring now yields a native editable Express document at true A2 and mixed canvases with real tables, a printed spec card converts into a live merge template, and an ink-level trace off a photographed tag recovers a real wordmark. So this is that client's actual job: the identity is recovered rather than invented, the catalogue is a real per-reference run, and the editable source files they asked for exist.
client_one_liner: Our pieces were photographed across two bench sessions and do not sit together, the only surviving version of our wordmark is printed on an old swing tag, and the autumn appointment season opens in six weeks.
client_brief:
Maison Valcere, autumn appointment season

We are four people in one room above a bookshop in Montreal. Twenty two references in the current book, most of them made to order, sold by appointment and through a small number of stockists. This autumn everything a client sees changes at once.

The honest state of our pictures. The pieces were photographed on the bench across two sessions, one in April and one in June, on the same pale sweep. Each frame is a good photograph on its own. Lay a row of them out the way a page does and they are not one house: some sit cooler, and the polished white gold does not read the same from one session to the other. We need them to read as one book. Clean white behind them, the piece centred, nothing touching the edge, no shadows invented for them. We also need versions with nothing behind them at all, because our stockists drop pieces onto a dark band of their own.

Then the wordmark. The original artwork left with the designer who set it, ten years ago. All that survives is a photograph of an old printed swing tag. We need it back as artwork the packer can hand to the die cutter, and working everywhere else too, at the size it actually sits on a boutique tile and reversed on our black.

What we need built. A house-story deck for stockists and press, carrying our materials and carat table honestly, one row per reference. Three poster directions at A2 for the room and the two fairs, in one file so we can choose between them. Boutique tiles for each piece. A launch social set, square and tall, in one file we can change ourselves. And a spec card for every reference in the book, one card per reference for the appointment folder, printed off the card our printer already uses.

Our pieces are nine hundred to six thousand five hundred dollars. Our clients are thirty five to sixty and they are buying for a marriage or a milestone. It should read quiet, black, a lot of held space, one object at a time. Not a mall counter and not a sale. And a note on what you did and anything we should know about using the wordmark.
price_band_and_audience: Appointment-led fine jewellery at 900 to 6,500 dollars a piece, buyers 35 to 60, purchase occasion a marriage or a milestone. The band is load-bearing. At this price the grammar is one object per canvas, deep held space, a near-black ground, high-contrast neoclassical type at a restrained scale, and the price shown discreetly or not at all. The same twenty two references at a 90 dollar mall band would correctly be laid out dense, four pieces to a tile, on white with a saturated accent, price set large beside a strike-through, and shipping that treatment here reads as a clearance counter and destroys the appointment premise the whole house rests on. Push the other way into pure vitrine minimalism with no copy and no table and the deck stops doing the job a stockist needs it to do, which is to answer metal, stone and carat without asking. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A posted job of this shape runs 2,000 to 4,500 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Independent fine-jewellery house, made to order and sold by appointment, with a small stockist channel.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2014, in a room above a bookshop in Montreal, Quebec. Four people, one bench.
brand_identity.about: Maison Valcere is a four-person high-jewellery house working to order for marriages and milestones. Twenty two references sit in the current book, most cut and set in-house and shown by appointment above the shop. The house sells quiet, considered pieces to clients who return once a decade, not once a season.
brand_identity.audience: Clients aged 35 to 60 buying for a marriage or a milestone, plus a short list of premium stockists. Considered, appointment-led buyers who research before they visit and expect the metal, stone and carat answered without asking.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Pieces run 900 to 6,500 dollars, positioned as appointment fine jewellery well above a mall counter and just below the named international maisons. Price is shown discreetly or not at all; the room and the book carry the value.
brand_identity.typography: Purely typographic, no symbols or icons. A high-contrast neoclassical serif with hairline serifs and a grave accent carries the wordmark and display; a restrained humanist or grotesque sans sets the specifications and body at a quiet scale. Generous letterspacing on caps, plenty of held space.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, precise, never salesy. States materials and provenance and stops. Example line: "Eighteen karat white gold, set with a single old-cut stone, made to your hand."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The original wordmark artwork left with the designer who set it a decade ago. The only surviving version is a photograph of an old printed swing tag, so the mark has to be recovered from that before it can be used again. No usable logo files, colour references or type spec survive; these guidelines are being reconstructed this season.
brand_identity.values: One object per canvas, honest materials, and a mark that reads as ours at every size. Restraint is the house, not decoration.

assets_supplied.name: valcere_bench/ (21 frames, 6960 x 4640)
assets_supplied.kind: Bench photography of the book shot across two sessions, April and June, one reference per frame on the same pale sweep.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Every piece in the book, same sweep, same bench. Two sittings, and I think the June ones went a touch cool."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: There are twenty one frames for twenty two references, because two of the frames are the same pendant shot from two angles and one reference was never photographed at all, which no filename and no column reveals. Separately the high-polish white gold pieces sit at almost the luminance of the sweep along the bezel shoulder, so the one-call knockout bites the edge exactly there while handing back a cutout that looks clean, complete and correct at preview scale.

assets_supplied.name: valcere_swing_tag.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of an old printed swing tag lying on a bench, the wordmark in one deep ink on pale board: high-contrast neoclassical caps with hairline serifs and a grave accent.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only place the wordmark still exists. The artwork went with the designer years ago."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The hairline serifs and the accent sit at the resolution floor of a handheld photograph of a small tag, so a trace that looks clean at canvas size closes those strokes at the size the mark actually reproduces on a tile and floods its counters when reversed on the house black. On the shadowed right of the tag the ink and the board also run close in value, so an ink-level selection loses strokes there before it loses them anywhere else.

assets_supplied.name: valcere_spec_card_PRINT.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The printer's existing spec card artwork, a real press PDF the house has been printing for two seasons, six printed lines plus a piece image.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The card our printer already runs. We just need it filled in for every reference."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The six lines were set as one continuous flow, so the conversion exposes a single story rather than the six addressable blocks the printed card suggests, and the mapping readout omits the assay line entirely while keeping its line break, so the string still looks well formed and every offset past it is short. The validator affirms those offsets as valid and the placeholder step reports success.

assets_supplied.name: valcere_book.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Twenty two rows: reference, piece name, metal, assay, stone, carat, band width, price, and a photo filename column.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The book as it stands. The assay line is regulated wording, it cannot be reworded."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: One reference's stone description runs several times longer than the rest, and the card's fixed text frame does not spill when it overflows, it simply stops rendering, so that record is truncated at trim while every response reports success. Two rows also carry the same photo filename.

assets_supplied.name: valcere_copy.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text: the house story, the provenance paragraph, the appointment copy and the stockist boilerplate.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The words as we say them. The provenance paragraph is the one we are not changing."

acceptance_bar: The twenty two references read as ONE book when laid in a row the way a page lays them: one white point, one black point, one crop logic, one height in frame. A frame that cannot be brought to the set is named, not shipped at eighty percent.
No delivered file exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions, and no crop or knockout tradeoff record in the run carries an upscale entry.

Boutique tiles sit square on a clean white ground with the piece optically centred and clear air at every edge, and the cut edge holds under close inspection on the high-polish pieces as well as the matte ones.
The transparent variants carry genuine alpha, so a piece dropped on a stockist's dark band shows no white plate and no bitten shoulder.
Every reference in the book has its own photograph, and no photograph stands in for two references. Where that cannot be met, the gap is named rather than filled.

The wordmark is placeable artwork rather than a picture of artwork: transparent, scalable with a real viewBox present, no opaque full-canvas rectangle riding underneath, and it still reads as our wordmark at the size it actually reproduces on a tile and reversed on our black.

The spec card run has one card per reference in the book, in book order, with every field on every card fully present at trim. A card that reaches the printer missing a line, or with a line stopped part way, fails even if the file opens.
In the deck the materials and carat table is a real table with one row per reference, not a picture of a table, and the words are text we can retype.
The three A2 poster directions sit in ONE working file at true A2, and the social canvases keep their own sizes in their own file, with the self-contained sources delivered alongside.
One type system across every canvas and the card run, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer and the actual weight used.

The note states, per photograph, what was applied and why that frame differs from its neighbours, plus every resize any tool reported, the reconciliation of frames against the book, and anything we should know about using the wordmark.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including image_vectorize which is counted HERE and not as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_fill_area, image_remove_background (transparent and backgroundColor routes), image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs and upscale_factor), image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Every raster decision in the commission. It fixes one house target off the best-lit sitting and corrects each frame toward it one call at a time, triages the knockout route between the matte pieces and the high-polish ones whose bezel shoulder shares luminance with the sweep, produces both the white-ground boutique tiles and the genuinely transparent variants the stockist band needs, prepares the per-reference piece images the card run binds, and recovers the wordmark at ink level off a photographed tag with the vector hygiene the tracing tool does not perform.

adobe_surfaces.surface: InDesign layout, merge-template authoring, data merge and print render
adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt (readout and validator), prepare_indd_merge_template (params.mappingJson as a JSON string), document_merge_data_layout (recordRange, additionalImageFiles, application/pdf and application/x-indesign), document_render_layout (createSeparateFiles, resolution)
adobe_surfaces.role: The per-reference spec card run off the printer's own press PDF. It converts the card, exports IDML to see what the conversion actually exposes, computes every text offset against the true story text, builds the merge template, binds the per-reference piece image through an at-prefixed CSV column, and delivers one press file with one record per page plus per-reference cards named to the book, with proofs rendered at real resolution rather than out of the merge itself.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The house-story deck with its real materials table, the three A2 poster directions in one document at true physical size, and the social canvases in a mixed-canvas document. Every photograph must be pulled down and inlined as image data because a URL renders as an empty grey box at full success, the wordmark goes in as inline SVG so it stays vector, family and weight are declared on every text element, each root declares its own canvas, and the payload goes by uploaded URL because inlined photography passes the inline threshold immediately.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: The one type system carried across the deck, the posters, the social set and the handover. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to land on quiet neoclassical rather than boutique-sale. Numeric weights are non-standard per family and cannot be inferred from a style name, a display cut is reached by its own slug rather than by weight, every name must be laundered into canonical PostScript form because one bad name kills the whole kit, and the CSS must use the returned slug or it falls back silently.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (entityScope StockAsset, SHORT query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the one frame the house does not have, a quiet dark interior ground for the poster directions, IP-clean, at genuine camera scale and with generative-tech candidates excluded, then graded into the same world as the bench set rather than dropped in as bought. The Boards half persists the selects set the four partners sign off from, placed within the twelve-per-call cap, with a partial success read as partial and vector understood to be unacceptable there.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching a pixel.
trajectory.judgement: The tiles and the piece images are raster work with a hard spec, the card run is a genuine record-per-page volume job and belongs on the merge surface, and the deck, posters and social have to be authored fixed canvases because the house needs to edit them next season. The brief pins all three destinations, so there is nothing here to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming a surface per deliverable, and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline: a manifest keyed by role, because sixty artefacts later the agent still has to know which URL is which reference.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Preview all twenty one bench frames and triage them: which sitting each belongs to, which sit cool, which pieces are high polish, which subjects run close to the sweep in value, and which reference each frame actually shows against the book.
trajectory.judgement: The house asserts a frame per reference. The pictures are the only place that can be settled, and reading frames against the book is slower than counting files and is not the same thing.
trajectory.produces: A per-frame triage note covering sitting, illuminant, polish, subject contrast against the ground, and reference identity.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level, before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes the subject and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Fix one house target off the best-lit frame and correct each frame toward it with its own call, recording the parameters applied.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a book, not twenty one good photographs. One batched call applies one identical parameter set, which is exactly wrong for two sittings under different light; the agent has to hold one destination and reach it by different routes.
trajectory.produces: Graded masters at source scale with a per-frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Masked corrections where a whole-frame move goes wrong, selecting the material by its own visual properties rather than by the object it sits on.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the whole gate: naming the substrate pulls the selection to the sweep. The yellow gold and the coloured stones need confined corrections the plain white gold does not.
trajectory.produces: Corrected frames where a global move would have taken the gold green or the sweep muddy.

trajectory.action: Knock the pieces out: a clean white ground for the boutique tiles and genuinely transparent variants for the stockist band, reading every returned tradeoffs object rather than the success message.
trajectory.judgement: The tradeoffs array is the only channel that reports what the tool did to a frame's dimensions and it carries no warning language. The high-polish bezels will not behave like the matte pieces.
trajectory.produces: White-ground plates and transparent variants, each with its returned tradeoffs recorded.

trajectory.action: Cut the boutique tiles square, hero and detail, the piece optically centred with clear air at every edge, and cut the small per-reference piece image the card run will bind.
trajectory.judgement: Optical centring is not geometric centring on a pendant hanging from a bail, and the tiles reject anything touching the edge. The card image is a different crop from the tile crop and has to be decided as its own thing.
trajectory.produces: Boutique tiles at spec, transparent variants, and a per-reference card image set named to the book.

trajectory.action: Recover the wordmark off the swing tag: an ink-level selection naming the mark's own visual properties, correct polarity, a bounds crop from the selection's own bbox, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full-canvas ground path removed.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions the tools do not make: how to word the selection so it takes the ink and not the board, which polarity to trace, and whether the two-colour trace or a colour-accurate knockout plate is what the die cutter should receive. Background removal is the wrong instrument on lettering.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent wordmark plus a colour-accurate variant, and the file intended for the die cutter.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's, judged against a 900 to 6,500 dollar appointment band and a milestone buyer. The weight cannot be inferred from the style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one-kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Convert the printer's spec card, export IDML, and look at what the conversion actually exposes as frames before promising any mapping.
trajectory.judgement: The printed card looks like six blocks, but frame granularity from a PDF is not under anybody's control. Exporting and reading is the only honest basis for a mapping.
trajectory.produces: An .indd, an .idml, and a written frame inventory with bounds, typography and existing links.

trajectory.action: Generate the mapping readout, build the mapping for every field in the book, validate it, then prepare the merge template and re-export IDML to confirm which placeholders actually landed.
trajectory.judgement: A success message from the placeholder step is not evidence that a placeholder exists. The only evidence is the round-tripped story text.
trajectory.produces: A merge template with a placeholder audit taken from the re-exported IDML rather than from the tool response.

trajectory.action: Merge the book: one press file with one record per page in book order, plus per-reference cards named to the reference through a route whose identity is guaranteed, binding the per-reference piece image through the at-prefixed column.
trajectory.judgement: Page count equal to row count is the checkable claim. Per-record identity is a route choice, not a naming choice, and a naive agent will place one static image on every record.
trajectory.produces: A press file with one card per reference and a per-reference card set named to the book.

trajectory.action: Render sign-off proofs at real resolution from the merged document rather than out of the merge call.
trajectory.judgement: Resolution asked for inside the merge is silently ignored, so a proof taken there is a screen-scale file wearing a print label.
trajectory.produces: Proofs at genuine resolution for the partners to read at trim.

trajectory.action: Author the house-story deck as one self-contained HTML: six roots, the materials and carat table as a real table with one row per reference, every photograph inlined as image data, the wordmark as inline SVG in an explicitly sized top-left anchored wrapper, family and weight declared on every text element.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, and an auto-sized right-anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas. The design work is how much held space the appointment band takes and how large the wordmark sits above one object.
trajectory.produces: An export-ready deck HTML, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Author the campaign document: three poster roots at true A2 in physical units plus the square and tall social roots, each root declaring its own canvas, carrying the same kit and the same wordmark treatment.
trajectory.judgement: Three directions means three genuinely different arguments, not one layout recoloured. A global canvas override is what collapses a mixed-size set, so the sizes are declared per root and nothing is passed as a parameter.
trajectory.produces: An export-ready campaign HTML carrying the poster directions and the social canvases.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check before each export, export both documents by uploaded URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve each document's rendition and look at its first root, and parse the returned per-root markup for every other root.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition preview only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at page one is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: Two native editable Express documents, two inspected first roots, and a per-root markup audit for the rest.

trajectory.action: Create the selects board, add the graded set, the tiles and the licensed ground within the per-call placement cap, re-sending only the entries the response names as failed, then write the handover note.
trajectory.judgement: A 201 is partial success, and the vector wordmark is not boardable so it belongs in the note instead. The note has to be specific enough that the next freelancer does not repeat the archaeology.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the card run actually carries the fields it reports carrying. The printer's six lines were set as one continuous flow, and the mapping readout hands back a story string that omits the regulated assay run while keeping its line break, so the string still reads as well formed and every offset past it is short by the length of the omission. The validator returns valid with no warnings on those offsets, the placeholder step reports completed successfully, and the merge produces a full set of cards. Only the merged pages show that the metal and reference lines never became placeholders and came through as the printer's original static wording on every card, identical for all twenty two references.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because nothing announces that the readout is lossy and every response in the chain affirms the wrong offsets, so there is no signal to order around. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that the printer's card should be filled in for every reference, and the acceptance line about no card reaching the printer missing a line is the house's standing trade requirement, not a disclosure. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is to compute offsets from a different source entirely, the true story text reconstructed from the document's own stories, which is a route the agent has no reason to take while the cheap readout is being validated as correct.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reconstruct the true story text from the document's stories, recompute every offset against it, rebuild the mapping, prepare the template again, re-export and confirm every expected field is present as a placeholder before any card is merged, then re-merge the book and read the long stone record at trim rather than at thumbnail scale.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Twenty two spec cards that arrive at the printer with the same metal and reference on every one of them, sent into a run whose only reason to exist is that each card is different.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered wordmark still reads as the house's wordmark once it sits at the size it actually reproduces on the real ground. The trace is taken from a handheld photograph of a small printed tag, so the hairline serifs and the grave accent sit at the resolution floor of that capture. At canvas size the traced paths look correct and complete. What the strokes do at boutique-tile size on the house black, and what the counters do when the mark is reversed out of that black rather than sitting on white, is a property of this particular capture and this particular trace and is visible only once the mark is placed at reproduction size on the actual ground.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) There is no ordering that avoids it and no parameter that prevents it, because the tracing tool takes no options at all and every lever is upstream in the raster preparation. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for the wordmark back as artwork for the die cutter and working at tile size and reversed on black, which is the house's requirement, not a warning that it will not. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different decision about which artwork carries which surface, and where necessary a differently prepared plate feeding the trace.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-derive the trace from a differently prepared plate, a higher-contrast ink-level selection or a filled colour-accurate plate rather than a binary mask, judge the result at reproduction size on the black rather than at canvas size, and where the hairlines still will not hold, split the system: the traced artwork for the die cutter at its own scale, a type-set lockup for the small sizes, with the split declared in the note.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A house whose wordmark is legible only on the one canvas somebody happened to look at, appearing on every boutique tile and every reversed panel as a smudged block with its accent gone, on an identity whose entire claim is that it is purely typographic.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the two constructs the Valcere look is built on. The house look is a deep black ground with one object held in a soft luminous falloff, and a hairline display line on the posters. Authored the natural way, the falloff is a blur and the hairline line is stroke-only type, and the importer discards a blur filter outright and resolves stroke-only type to a fully transparent colour, both with no warning and a successful response. The returned per-root markup is the only channel that reports either, and each document's rendition returns its first root only, so the five other deck roots and the two other poster directions can be checked no other way.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and the import is the last step, and doing it right first time presumes knowing which of several plausible constructions survives, which no tool reports. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for a look and the acceptance lines are about how the work reads, not about what an importer keeps. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is to build the falloff differently, as a radial gradient shape or as part of the raster by knocking the piece onto a house ground so the falloff is pixels, and to set the display line as solid type with tracking, then re-compose around whichever it is.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the affected masters through a different route, re-author both documents around what actually survives, re-run the readiness check, re-export, and audit every root from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A deck and a poster set delivered as editable files in which the pieces sit on flat black with hard edges and the poster display line is invisible on the two directions nobody looked at, with every export having reported success.

deliverables.name: Maison Valcere house photography
deliverables.spec: The bench frames brought to one house target, one white point, one black point, one crop logic, one height in frame, across two sittings, plus one licensed camera-scale interior ground graded into the same world. Per-frame parameter log with one line on why each frame differs from its neighbours, and a written reconciliation of frames against the twenty two references in the book.

deliverables.name: Boutique tile set, white ground and on-band
deliverables.spec: Square boutique tiles per reference on a clean white ground, hero and detail, the piece optically centred with clear air at every edge and a cut edge that holds under close inspection on high-polish pieces as well as matte ones, plus genuinely transparent variants for the stockists' dark band. Every output at or below its source pixel dimensions with the returned tradeoff record for each. One set with one cut logic, not one picture at several sizes.

deliverables.name: Recovered Valcere wordmark
deliverables.spec: The wordmark recovered from a photograph of a printed swing tag as placeable scalable vector geometry with a transparent ground: a real viewBox present, no opaque full-canvas rectangle riding along, delivered as the file the die cutter receives and as a colour-accurate variant, holding at the size it actually reproduces on a boutique tile and reversed out of the house black, with any split between traced artwork and type-set lockup stated.

deliverables.name: Spec card run for the book
deliverables.spec: One press file carrying one card per reference in book order, page count equal to row count, built off the printer's own card artwork, with every field present at trim on every card including the regulated assay wording and the long stone record, the per-reference piece image bound per row rather than one static image repeated, plus per-reference cards named to the reference and sign-off proofs rendered at genuine resolution.

deliverables.name: House-story deck and campaign document, plus their sources
deliverables.spec: Two native editable Express documents: a six-root house-story deck whose materials and carat table is a real table with one row per reference, and a campaign document carrying three genuinely different A2 poster directions at true physical size alongside the square and tall social canvases, each root keeping its own canvas. Live editable text in one licensed type system, the wordmark as real vector shapes, every photograph carried as embedded image data. Delivered with the self-contained source HTML, which is the durable half.

deliverables.name: Handover note and selects board
deliverables.spec: A written note recording per photograph what was applied and why that frame differs from its neighbours, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and the actual numeric weight, every resize any tool reported with the frame it applied to, the frame-to-book reconciliation including any reference that has no photograph, what the card run does and does not carry, and everything the house should know about using the wordmark at size and reversed. Paired with a persistent shareable selects board with nothing silently dropped.

verifiers_auto.text: The spec card press file has exactly as many pages as the book has references, in book order.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the page count of the delivered press file and compare it against the row count of the supplied CSV, then read the reference on each page in order.

verifiers_auto.text: Every mapped field became a real placeholder in the merge template, including the regulated assay line.
verifiers_auto.how: Round-trip the prepared template to IDML and grep the stories for each expected field token, asserting none is absent.

verifiers_auto.text: No two merged cards carry the same metal, assay and reference values unless the book itself repeats them, and no card's text stops part way through a line.
verifiers_auto.how: Extract the text of each page of the press file and diff it row by row against the CSV, flagging identical field values across records and any value that is a prefix of its source string.

verifiers_auto.text: No delivered file exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions and no tradeoff record in the run carries an upscale entry.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the pixel dimensions of every delivered file against the frame it derives from per the manifest, and diff the captured tradeoffs objects against the resize table in the note.

verifiers_auto.text: The transparent variants carry genuine alpha rather than a white plate.
verifiers_auto.how: Inspect the alpha channel of each variant for partial-alpha pixels at the piece boundary and full transparency at the frame corners.

verifiers_auto.text: The recovered wordmark SVG has a viewBox attribute and no full-canvas opaque background path at path index zero.
verifiers_auto.how: Parse the delivered SVG: assert a viewBox is present and assert the first path's geometry does not span the whole canvas.

verifiers_auto.text: Both exports returned the expected number of roots, each keeping its own declared canvas size, with the poster roots at true A2 dimensions.
verifiers_auto.how: Read slide_count and the per-slide width and height in each export response.

verifiers_auto.text: No image in any root resolved to the importer's placeholder, the wordmark arrived as vector path shapes, the materials table arrived as a real table, and every text element carries a resolved licensed face.
verifiers_auto.how: Parse the returned per-root markup for placeholder image data, count path shapes in the wordmark region, assert table row and cell elements equal to the reference count, and check every font-family against the families the kit call returned.

verifiers_human.text: Every card in the appointment folder is complete at trim, including the longest stone description.
verifiers_human.how: Read the proofs at trim size, card by card, against the book.

verifiers_human.how: View the three roots together and judge whether each would be chosen for a different reason.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are raster work, which are a genuine record-per-page run, and which need an authored fixed-canvas document, given that only one surface composes free-form layout and only one does volume personalisation.
Whether the two bench sittings are one book. The house believes they nearly are; the row is the only place that can be settled.
How far to push the cooler sitting before it stops being worth saving, versus naming it.

Knockout route per piece: the one-call route for matte coherent pieces versus a material-named sweep selection inverted and filled for the high-polish bezels whose shoulder shares luminance with the ground.
Whether twenty one frames for twenty two references is a filename problem or a photography gap, and how to say so when it is the second.
Selection prompt wording on the swing tag: naming the substrate takes the board, naming the ink's own visual properties takes the mark, and the shadowed side loses strokes before the lit side does.

Which wordmark artwork carries which surface, judged at reproduction size on the actual ground rather than at full canvas, and whether the die cutter and the tiles should receive the same file at all.
What the converted card actually exposes as mappable structure, and what a mapping can honestly promise once that is known.
Which merge route guarantees per-reference identity for the named card set, given that a per-record route that looks like the obvious one is not the one that guarantees it.

The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against an appointment band and a milestone buyer, plus the real numeric weight per family and whether the display cut is reached by slug.
How much held space the deck and the posters carry. At this band restraint is the design, and a dense, benefit-led layout is a correct-looking wrong answer.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of jewellery. IDENTITY: these are this house's actual twenty two references with their actual metals, stones and regulated assay wording, and the wordmark must be RECOVERED off a photographed swing tag rather than reinvented, because a regenerated wordmark is a different house's identity and a redrawn ring is not the ring the client will hand over. SPEC: the stockists need square tiles at an exact size with nothing touching the edge and no interpolated pixels plus transparent variants for their own dark band, the printer needs one card per reference in book order off their own existing artwork with every regulated line present at trim, and none of that is satisfiable or checkable in a generated image. EDITABILITY: the deck, the posters and the social set are defined by being editable, since the book changes every season and a four-person house cannot re-commission. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did this placeholder actually land, does this card carry a different reference from the last one, does this wordmark still read at the size it reproduces.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and upscale_factor, fill_area, remove_background in both the transparent and backgroundColor forms, and vectorize are verified headless across 27 live calls; the substrate-versus-ink prompt asymmetry, the missing viewBox and the opaque path zero are live findings, and alpha survives crops at outputFileType png (13,371 partial-alpha pixels preserved), so the on-band variants are real. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout and document_render_layout are all verified fully headless and synchronous end to end, a card PDF was reverse-engineered into a live merge template, PDF output is one record per page with page count equal to row count, per-row image binding through an at-prefixed column plus additionalImageFiles is visually confirmed, per-record identity is guaranteed by createSeparateFiles or a recordRange loop, and document_render_layout returns true 300 dpi while outputSpecs.resolution inside the merge is silently ignored. The card checkpoint rests on the documented lossy-textContent finding: a 17-character run was dropped while its line break was kept, every later offset was short by exactly 17, the validator returned VALID with zero warnings, prepare reported success, and only 3 of 5 mappings landed. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export, true physical units at 96 dpi, real tables with per-cell shapes and text, inline SVG as native editable vector, and a genuine editable dcx findable by asset_search are all verified, filter blur is dropped and webkit-text-stroke resolves to a fully transparent colour at HTTP success, and the rendition preview is documented as first root only, which is why verification is split between the rendition and the returned markup. Transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined photography passes the 70 KB threshold immediately. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit verified end to end, including the all-or-nothing kit call, non-standard numeric weights and slug-not-PostScript CSS. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed, license returned a real 7360x4912 JPEG, boards persist with a hard cap of 12 placements per call and 201 meaning partial. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no variable QR, no bleed or press-preset claim, no upscaling, no compositing, no OCR, no text-to-image, no fill_text, no animate_design, no photo reaching Express as a URL, no batch above 20.
